title: Apple Inc. — Annual Report (SYNTHETIC FIXTURE for offline demo/evals)
body:
SYNTHETIC FIXTURE — This document is an invented excerpt in the style of a 10-K, bundled for offline demos and evaluation. Its figures are fictional and must not be used as financial data.

ITEM 1. BUSINESS

Apple Inc. designs, manufactures and markets smartphones, personal computers, tablets, wearables and accessories, and sells a variety of related services. The Company's fiscal 2025 net sales were $402.1 billion, an increase of 5 percent year over year. iPhone remains the largest product category with net sales of $205.3 billion. The Services segment, which includes the App Store, iCloud, Apple Music, Apple TV+ and payment services, generated $96.2 billion in net sales, growing 12 percent year over year and representing the Company's fastest-growing major segment. The Company distributes its products through its retail and online stores, direct sales force, and third-party cellular network carriers, wholesalers and resellers.

ITEM 1A. RISK FACTORS

The Company's global supply chain is concentrated in Asia, and a majority of final assembly is performed by a small number of outsourcing partners, principally in China, India and Vietnam. Disruption at any of these partners could materially and adversely affect product availability. Regulatory developments also present material risk: the European Union's Digital Markets Act has required changes to App Store distribution and payment terms in the European Union, and further regulatory or judicial determinations in other jurisdictions could reduce Services revenue. The Company also faces intense competition in all of its markets, and rapid change in artificial intelligence technologies could alter competitive dynamics in ways the Company cannot fully predict.

ITEM 7. MANAGEMENT'S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS

Gross margin for fiscal 2025 was 46.1 percent, compared with 45.0 percent in fiscal 2024, reflecting a favourable mix shift toward Services. Research and development expense was $31.4 billion, an increase of 9 percent, driven by headcount and infrastructure supporting silicon engineering and machine-learning features. During fiscal 2025 the Board of Directors authorised an additional $90 billion for the share repurchase programme. The Company declared and paid aggregate dividends of $15.2 billion during the year. The Company ended the fiscal year with $62.5 billion in cash and cash equivalents and continues to target a net-cash-neutral position over time.
